sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.1250 of 2024
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Roads & Buildings appearing for respondent No.1, Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for respondent No.2, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondents No.3 to 5, and perused the record.

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioner, in brief, is that part of the land belonging to his wife i.e., to an extent of Ac.0-10 guntas 102 sq. yards = 1554 sq. yards, in survey No.85 situated at Venkatadripalem Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, Nalgonda District, was acquired by the respondents for the formation of railway line from Bibi Nagar to Nadekude, no compensation is paid for the said land and on the other hand, the respondents-authorities are now claiming that the compensation amount payable for the said land has been deposited before the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') under Award proceedings,
dt.22.09.1986 vide O.P.No.32 of 1988 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Mirayalaguda at Nalgonda District, which action it is contended as highly illegal and arbitrary.
3.

Per contra, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondents No.3 to 5 submits that since, the original claimant i.e., wife of the petitioner being aggrieved by the Award passed by the respondents- authorities had joined the O.P. filed by other claimants as claimant No.9 vide O.S.No.32 of 1988 on the file of the Senior civil Judge, Miryalaguda at Nalgonda District, the authorities have deposited the amount payable to the credit of the aforesaid O.P.
4.

Learned Government Pleader further submits that since, the amount has already been deposited into the Court in terms of Section 30 of the Act, the petitioner is required to approach the concerned Civil Court to withdraw the compensation amount.
5. I have taken note of the respective submissions made.

6. Though the petitioner claims that part of the land belonging to his wife having been acquired without paying any compensation, however, as the respondents- authorities claim of passing of the Award dt.22.09.1986, the claim of the petitioner that the land belonging to his wife having been acquired without passing any award and payment of compensation cannot be accepted as valid Cheedalla Murali vs The State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104992373/
1 claim.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the petitioner's wife, who is the land owner and whose property has been acquired under the award having joined as claimant No.9 in the O.P. preferred by the other claimants vide O.S.No.32 of 1988 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Miryalaguda at Nalgonda District and the respondents on filing of case having deposited the amount payable in respect of the land acquired under the award before the Civil Court in terms of Sections 30 & 31 of the Act

, this Court is of the view that the petitioner should be directed to approach the Civil Court seeking withdrawal of the amount deposited by the respondents as per the Award, dt.22.09.1986, to which the petitioner's wife, who is claimed to have deceased in the year 2012, is entitled in terms of the said award.
8.
Subject to the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
9. Consequently, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
